drug_class: Colony-stimulating factor (a type of white blood cell booster)
purpose: Filgrastim-sndz helps your body make more white blood cells, which are the cells that fight infection. It is often used in people who have low white blood cell counts due to chemotherapy, bone marrow transplants, or certain other medical conditions. By boosting your white blood cells, it helps lower your risk of getting serious infections.
how_it_works: Your body naturally makes a protein called G-CSF that tells your bone marrow to produce white blood cells. This medication is a man-made version of that protein, so it sends the same signal to your bone marrow. Think of it like giving your bone marrow a nudge to work harder and make more infection-fighting cells.
common_side_effects: Bone or muscle aches and pain (especially in the lower back, hips, or legs) are the most common side effects. You may also experience headache, tiredness, nausea, or redness and soreness at the injection site.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you have sudden or worsening pain in your upper left belly or shoulder, as this could be a sign of a serious spleen problem. Rarely, it can cause a severe allergic reaction, lung problems, or a condition where the tiny air sacs in the lungs fill with fluid. Also let your doctor know if you have sickle cell disease, as this medication can sometimes cause a sickle cell crisis.
typical_dosing: The dose depends on why you are taking it and your body weight. It is given as an injection either under the skin (subcutaneous) or into a vein (IV). Your doctor or nurse will determine the right dose and schedule for you, which may be once a day or on specific days around your chemotherapy treatment.
